independence.priorParticipation: This is the second consecutive cycle in which I review a repair of my own objection, and in this lineage my footprint is now threefold: the subject pins my verdict on its parent as parentReview, pins my verdict on its predecessor as predecessorV1.review, and exists to land a SHOULD-FIX I wrote. An artifact built this closely around one reviewer's findings is the hardest thing to review honestly, because agreement feels like verification. Four guards. First, I graded the repair against the corpus rather than against myself: the test was whether the pass semantics matched the parent's own executesIfRecorded byte for byte and whether the per-class shape matched the sibling that already uses it, both of which a repair written only from my prose would have failed. Second, I ran a dedicated over-correction pass, since a successor landing a finding can fail by doing too much — checking that nothing was executed, that no platform or number was added, and that the pass semantics were sourced rather than composed. Third, I recomputed every v1 measurement instead of carrying it forward, including re-hashing all seventeen fixtures. Fourth, I verified my own two pinned verdicts as citations like any other, including that the standing v2 attributes to them — ACCEPT 0/0 and REJECT 0/1 — is what those files actually record. What I still cannot self-certify is whether a reviewer with no stake here would have found something in the new 36,000 bytes that I did not; the coordinator should weigh that, and a Codex pass on this subject would be worth more than usual.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-six attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 851abb4d at 0444, 54672 bytes, unmoved at both ends; predecessor v1 unmoved at 3202bdd5 and not overwritten; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified with DR-G31 occurring zero times in either. All eleven cited pins reproduce, including the two that are my own verdicts. The v1 SHOULD-FIX is landed substantively. passProperty now carries, by name, the two consequences I identified: each of the eleven primaries must reproduce its D-130 pinned digest and produce its expected fate, and a run executing zero classes or producing no report fails. failsIf holds twenty-six entries, two of which state those same conditions as failures, and one of which makes the artifact's own completeness a failure condition. Every one of the eleven classes now carries exactByteIntent and passProperty, and each evidence member states that the runner must recompute the digest from disk. Crucially the semantics are sourced rather than composed: executesWhenRun.ruleVerbatim is byte-equal to naming v1's gate.executesIfRecorded, the very field I reported v1 had left behind, so this is a carry-forward rather than a paraphrase of my finding. I ran a separate over-correction pass because a successor landing a finding can fail by doing too much: nothing is executed, no platform or number is added, the matrix arithmetic recomputes to its stated 44, and 'pass all four D-002 platforms' follows from the stated matrix plus the parent's own 'pass all' waiver rule. I also re-ran every v1 measurement rather than carrying it forward — all seventeen fixtures re-hashed from disk and reproducing, class order and field-by-field agreement with D-130 intact, no twelfth class, no status recorded — and confirmed the repair is strictly additive on all eleven class records, with the nine changed top-level keys each explained by the successor act. Two further checks came back clean: OBL-G31-HARNESS-SPEC is not minted here, existing already in identity-namespace-leftover-join.v3 and following a seventeen-strong sibling pattern; and predecessorV1 describes my v1 verdict exactly as REJECT 0/1 under the right finding id without softening what was missing. whatThisCloses is more conservative than the parent, recording gates2and3Hold false. One observation for the coordinator, outside this subject and not a finding: identity-namespace-leftover-join.v3 already names OBL-G31-HARNESS-SPEC while G31 exists only as a proposal absent from file 08; I found this while establishing the identifier's provenance, did not open that join's review, and take no position on it. Finally, the disclosure that matters most here. This is the second consecutive cycle in which I review a repair of my own objection, and my footprint in this lineage is now threefold — the subject pins my verdict on its parent, pins my verdict on its predecessor, and exists to land my SHOULD-FIX. I graded against the corpus rather than against myself, ran the over-correction pass, recomputed rather than carried forward, and verified my own pinned verdicts as citations. What I cannot self-certify is whether a reviewer with no stake would have found something in the new thirty-six thousand bytes that I did not. A Codex pass on this subject would be worth more than usual.
